messages.subject: "overlaid forest plots with ancillary data)
parts:
I have a dataframe with effects sizes for a load of studies, upper and lower bounds for the effects and ancillary data (sample size, event rate). I have data from two sources coded via availability.
ie vector with trial name. vector with effect size, vector with upper ci, lower ci, sample size, event rate,  & availability
I want to do three things. 
Firstly i want a forest plot of the data from one source...I'm almost there with this but the order of the studies is reversed (how do i get the x axis in reverse numeric order?). 
Secondly i want to add facets  displaying the control group event rate and sample size against a common x axis.
Finally I want to display the data from the two sources in different colors, something like color = factor(availability)?

code to date below

# Create data.
d <- data.frame(x = dat$cummulative.evidence,y = dat$cumulative.RR, ylo=dat$lower.ci, yhi=dat$upper.ci, availability=dat$availability, size=dat$N, event rate=dat$event.rate)


forestplot <- function(d, xlab="Risk Ratio", ylab=""){
  require(ggplot2)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, ymin=ylo, ymax=yhi, colour=factor(availability))) + 
    geom_pointrange() + 
    coord_flip() +
    geom_hline(aes(x=0), lty=2) +
    ylab(xlab) +
    xlab(ylab) +#switch because of the coord_flip() above
    ylim(0,3)
  return(p)
}

forestplot(d)

happy to add more detail- if anyone can help....
